Effects of Jet Plume on Hypersonic Sonic Boom of Slender Bodies
recent_works.abstract: The jet plume effects on sonic boom for hypersonic slender bodies are studied systematically for the first time by simulating nose cone and nose double-cone geometries. The jet plume effects on hypersonic sonic boom are found to be different from the effects on low-supersonic sonic boom because the significantly smaller leading shock angle makes the shock directly interact with the underexpanded jet plume. When sufficiently underexpanded, the jet-induced shocks and shear layers significantly amplify the peak overpressure by a factor of 2–3 at hypersonic flight conditions. A detailed analysis of the dependence of the jet plume effects on the static-pressure ratio, jet Mach number, and vehicle shape has been performed. The static-pressure ratio and jet Mach number are found to have a significant impact on the jet plume effects. The jet plume effects also show sensitivity to the vehicle shape when the static-pressure ratio is small. recent_works.title: Iso-surface sampler: Bayesian optimization-based sampling framework for controlling multi-fuel compression ignition engines
recent_works.abstract: Over the years, engines have been continuously improved to operate across a wide range of operating conditions and meet various requirements. This has led to an increase in actuators and their corresponding control inputs. Traditionally, to control the engine, maps are developed by human calibration. However, as the number of operating conditions and control inputs increases, this can be challenging. To overcome this, data-driven model-based frameworks have been proposed, assuming the existence of a dataset for model development. The accuracy of the developed controller depends on the accuracy of the model, and that in turn depends on the dataset used. However, developing extensive datasets sweeping across the entire range of operating conditions and control inputs can be challenging. In this paper, a sampling framework called the Iso-surface Sampler (ISS) is proposed for developing datasets with outputs within a desirable range, making them suitable for controller development. The proposed sampling framework uses knowledge of the underlying system and Bayesian optimization to build datasets. recent_works.title: Modeling of Plasma Ignition of Low Cetane Fuels in an Aerial Internal Combustion Engine
recent_works.abstract: Reliable ignition of low-cetane fuels under engine-relevant, lean, or low-temperature conditions remains a critical challenge for advanced aerial internal combustion systems. The present study numerically investigates low cetane (CN 17) alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) synthetic aviation fuel (SAF) ignition assisted by nanosecond repetitively pulsed (NRP) discharges, using a novel two-stage modeling framework. The plasma discharge is represented using a phenomenological model, which partitions each pulse’s energy into vibrational and electronic excitation of N2, where, the latter subsequently quenches, resulting in ultra-fast O2 dissociation and gas heating, thereby capturing the key thermal and non-thermal effects of NRP discharges in a computationally efficient manner. To enable tractable simulations with detailed chemistry, a reduced chemical kinetic model comprising 49 species was developed from a detailed CRECK mechanism using the Directed Relation Graph with Error Propagation (DRG-EP) technique, and was employed in all simulations presented in this study. recent_works.title: Drift-Diffusion Modeling of Non-equilibrium Plasma Streamers with Photoionization
recent_works.abstract: Non-equilibrium plasma streamers play a critical role in nanosecond pulsed discharges, plasma-assisted combustion enhancement, and plasma-based flow control, yet their accurate modeling requires a self-consistent treatment of electrodynamics, transport, and plasma chemistry. In this work, we present a drift-diffusion-convection framework for simulating plasma streamer propagation at atmospheric or higher pressures interacting with gas flows. An in-house OpenFOAM-based solver is developed from a reacting flow framework (originally for combustion simulation) to incorporate charged species equations, electron energy equation, Poisson’s equation of electrostatic potential, and photoionization models. The governing equations couple the compressible Navier–Stokes system with reacting multi-species transport, total enthalpy conservation, and plasma-specific source terms, while electron-impact kinetics and electron transport coefficients are evaluated using pre-tabulated rate coefficients generated by BOLSIG+.
